title: Deployment safety fence: fine-grained traffic constraints and geo-eviction for model variant rollouts
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: When rolling out new model variants across heterogeneous capacity tiers and regions, we observe spiky error/latency patterns and unexpected customer impact when traffic surges hit zones with partial compatibility. Current policies (weighted canaries + simple failover) lack a fine-grained safety fence that can both constrain traffic per-dimension (region, tier, customer SLA) and evict or quarantine problematic variants automatically without global rollback.

Goal: Implement a deployment safety fence that: (1) enforces multi-dimensional traffic constraints during rollouts (region, capacity tier, customer class), (2) detects short-lived, high-severity regressions and performs local eviction or quarantine of a variant (region/tier scoped) before escalating to full rollback, and (3) integrates with existing canary/AB/shadow plumbing so operators can configure policies via Console and observe decisions in tracing and dashboards.
acceptance_criteria: Operators can define per-variant traffic caps by region and capacity tier via Console (JSON policy or UI form)
Runtime enforces caps: actual routed traffic never exceeds policy thresholds under normal load and adjusts when autoscaling changes capacity
Automatic quarantine: variant enters a quarantined state for the specific region/tier if error-rate or latency regression exceeds configured thresholds for 3 consecutive 1-minute windows
Quarantine actions supported: traffic divert to primary variant, redirect to fallback variant, or shadow-only mode; action is configurable per policy
Eviction events are visible in Console with root-cause signals (latency percentiles, error types, sample requests) and a suggested remediation (roll forward, rollback, config tweak)
End-to-end tests and chaos tests demonstrate that local quarantine prevents global customer-impact while preserving healthy regions
Documentation page (Console + API) published with examples and recommended policies for PLG customers and enterprise tiers
design_notes: Policy model: simple declarative policy with dimensions {region, capacity_tier, customer_tier, route} and thresholds for error_rate, p95_latency, token_drop_rate
Local state machine: per-variant/per-scope status = {Active, Throttled, Quarantined, Evicted}; transitions driven by rolling window metrics and hysteresis to avoid flapping
Decision points: enforce caps at the routing layer (before admission) and trigger quarantine in the admission controller so KV cache and in-flight requests are treated consistently
Compatibility validation: pre-deploy compatibility probes from the staging mesh to target region/tier to catch deterministic incompatibilities (e.g., missing ops in quantized kernels)
Observability: emit events to tracing (trace tags: safety_fence.decision, variant_id, scope), and aggregate in Console timeline with sample request IDs and links to GitHub PR + eval set
Operator controls: immediate manual override via Console to lift quarantine, change action, or pin a different fallback
Performance: admission enforcement path should add <1.5ms median overhead; batching and caching of policy lookups required (LRU per-edge-router)
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (design + API): finalize policy schema and Console controls (2 weeks)
Phase 1 (runtime prototype): implement enforcement hooks in routing layer, add per-scope state machine, start emitting decision events (3 weeks)
Phase 2 (integration): connect quarantine actions to rollout engine (canary/AB), add rollback suggestions and expose in Console (2 weeks)
Phase 3 (canary): enable safety fence for internal canaries only, run 10 internal canaries across US/EMEA tiers, iterate thresholds (2 weeks)
Phase 4 (customer opt-in): announce as early access to enterprise customers and collect feedback (3 weeks)
Phase 5 (GA): enable default soft-enforcement for hosted API with sensible defaults and docs (1 week)
Rollback policy: quarantine escalation -> operator review -> automatic full rollback if global user-impact rises above 0.5% MAU-exposed error threshold
test_plan: Unit tests for policy parsing and validation (schema edge cases)
Integration tests: simulated multi-region router with synthetic traffic to validate caps and decision hysteresis
Chaos tests: inject cross-region latency spikes and simulated kernel incompatibility to ensure quarantine containment
Performance test: measure admission path latency overhead at QPS 10k and 100k with policy cache enabled
E2E canary: deploy to non-production workspace, run text generation and embedding traffic profiles, verify Console events and suggested remediations
Customer scenario tests: reproduce a legacy enterprise workload that failed in earlier rollouts (PR reference in comments)
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Overly aggressive quarantine could fragment capacity and harm throughput; Mitigation: use conservative default thresholds and require 3-window confirmation before quarantine
Risk: Policy lookup latency could add tail to admission; Mitigation: LRU cache and batched refreshes from config store
Risk: Operators may rely too heavily on automatic actions; Mitigation: Console warnings and require opt-in for auto-eviction for P0 customers
Risk: False positives from noisy telemetry; Mitigation: combine multiple signals (error type, p95, tokens) and require correlated anomalies
